FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.96
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox project context correctly. It writes only the patched target file into a temp directory and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that lone file path (`patched_path`). Any fix whose validity depends on sibling modules, package imports, pyright config, or repo-relative context is evaluated out of context. Evidence: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`; no package tree/config is copied; post-fix analysis calls `_count_tool_issues(run_pyright, patched_path)` etc. This can silently mark a harmful fix SAFE/NEUTRAL or a safe fix HARMFUL because imports/config resolution differ from the real codebase.
FOLLOW: This crosses the endocrine→immune interface because immune stage 4 uses `evaluate_fixes()` to set `finding.verified = True`. A false SAFE/NEUTRAL verdict closes bugs via NK bug-closed gating in later rounds and suppresses rediscovery. A false HARMFUL verdict rejects a correct first fix and keeps the bug open. In both directions the PoC reviewer gets misleading closure state, and the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” feature is not actually testing the fix in repo context.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — copy the full source tree needed for analysis into the temp directory, replace only the target file inside that copied tree, and run pyright/ruff/bandit from the temp project root against the copied relative path instead of against an isolated basename file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.94
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68
DESCRIPTION: FIND — optional test execution in `evaluate_fix()` is not run against the patched source. The code sets `cwd=tmpdir` but executes `test_cmd` unchanged. Immune stage 4 passes `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`. In the tempdir created by endocrine there is no copied `bench/` tree, so pytest either fails immediately or imports the original repository from elsewhere on `sys.path`, meaning tests do not exercise the patched file. Evidence: tempdir contains only `os.path.basename(target_path)`; no rewriting of `test_cmd`, no environment isolation, no copied tests/package tree.
FOLLOW: This makes the “tests_passed” signal mechanically unreliable. `_compute_fix_verdict()` treats `tests_passed is False` as HARMFUL and `tests_passed is True` as supporting SAFE. Because the tests are not bound to the sandboxed patch, verdicts can be wrong in either direction. Downstream, immune stage 4 may mark fixes verified based on unrelated test outcomes or reject fixes because pytest cannot locate the project. That directly affects canonical finding closure and end-to-end reviewer trust in fix evaluation.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when `test_cmd` is provided, copy the relevant project tree/tests into the temp directory and rewrite execution to run against that copied tree; if that is not done, disable test execution for sandbox eval and leave `tests_passed=None` rather than running misleading tests.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a fix as SAFE even when it leaves the original defect unchanged, because it compares only total counts before/after and does not verify that the target finding disappeared. Evidence: a fix reducing one unrelated ruff issue elsewhere in the file while leaving the reported bug intact yields `total_net < 0`, therefore SAFE. Likewise a no-op on the target bug with passing tests yields SAFE. There is no linkage from `finding` to a specific diagnostic code/location/message in the post-fix state.
FOLLOW: Immune stage 4 uses SAFE/NEUTRAL as proof that a finding’s fix is verified. If endocrine says SAFE for a fix that never resolved the claimed bug, the immune layer marks `finding.verified=True`, NK closes future duplicates, and the system reports a closed bug that still exists. This is a high-severity silent wrong-result path, not just a quality issue.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — require fix evaluation to prove non-regression relative to the specific target by checking that at least one diagnostic at the cited/targeted location or matching the finding description decreases/disappears; if target resolution cannot be established, return NEUTRAL instead of SAFE.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `EndocrineLayer.run()` claims the endocrine layer provides “defect detection — classify findings by defect category”, but `run()` and `EndocrineReport` never expose any separate defect-detection result beyond raw tool diagnostics. The categorisation helpers exist only inside tool runners, and there is no function that classifies round findings or emits defect-category summaries for insect brain consumption. This is a declared feature that never fires.
FOLLOW: The insect brain receives only `health_scan`, `fix_evaluations`, and `pacing_signals`. Any round-level decision logic that expects endocrine defect detection is impossible because no such output exists. At PoC stage that means one advertised endocrine capability is dead code / missing functionality, reducing end-to-end feature completeness for reviewer demonstration.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — either remove “Defect detection” from the module/API contract, or add a minimal exported summary in `EndocrineReport` that aggregates `health_scan.diagnostics` by `category` so the feature actually fires without adding new reasoning.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006
SEVERITY: 0.82
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_pyright()` records pyright line/column positions without converting from pyright’s zero-based coordinates to the one-based convention used by the other tool runners and by human-facing file references. Evidence: it sets `line=rng.get("line", 0)` and `column=rng.get("character", 0)` directly, while mypy/bandit/ruff all emit one-based locations. Pyright JSON uses zero-based `range.start.line` / `character`.
FOLLOW: Mixed indexing corrupts downstream per-diagnostic location semantics. Any reviewer or downstream logic comparing tool outputs by file/line can misalign pyright findings by one line, breaking deduplication, triage, and human navigation. In fix evaluation, if future logic ties findings to line locations, pyright-origin findings will appear unresolved or resolved incorrectly.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — add 1 to pyright `line` and `character` when non-null so `ToolDiagnostic` uses a consistent one-based convention across all tools.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F007
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can pick the wrong source file by substring containment: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. A short basename or partial path mentioned in prose can match multiple files, and the first hit wins. Evidence: no exact-normalized path resolution, no ambiguity detection, fallback to first source path.
FOLLOW: Wrong target selection means endocrine may read, patch, lint, and verdict a different file than the finding refers to. That makes fix evaluation results invalid while still looking successful. Downstream, immune stage 4 can mark the finding verified even though the real target file was untouched, closing the wrong bug.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — resolve only exact basename or normalized relative-path matches; if multiple source paths match, return `None` and mark the fix UNEVALUABLE instead of guessing.
VERIFIED: TRUE

The loop body wraps each runner call in `try/except`; on exception it logs, sets `tools_available[tool_name] = False`, and proceeds to the next tool. There is no whole-scan crash from a runner exception in the current code. The real bug in that block is false availability on NOT_FOUND, already captured by C0004/C0001.
